result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 






To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.




Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication makes a difference in people's lives.



About the Department


The Engineering and Facilities Management Department is responsible for ensuring Monash Health's hospitals and healthcare facilities remain safe, reliable, compliant and operational 24 hours a day. Supporting more than 40 sites across Victoria, the department delivers facilities management, engineering, maintenance, essential services compliance and operational support that enables high-quality patient care.


Our teams work closely with clinical services, engineering specialists, contractors and operational leaders to ensure hospital infrastructure and building services perform safely, efficiently and with minimal disruption to healthcare delivery.



About the Role


Join our team as the Senior Manager - Sites Operations on a full-time, ongoing basis, primarily based at Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, with regular travel across Monash Health sites.


Reporting to the Head of Engineering & Facilities Management, you will lead the site-based Facilities Management teams responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance and performance of Monash Health's buildings, infrastructure and engineering services.


As the operational lead for site facilities, you will ensure hospital infrastructure remains safe, compliant and reliable while working closely with clinical and operational stakeholders to minimise service disruptions and support the delivery of exceptional patient care.



Key responsibilities include:


Lead and develop multidisciplinary Facilities Management teams across assigned sites.
Oversee the delivery of planned, preventative and reactive maintenance programs.
Ensure compliance with statutory requirements, essential services regulations and organisational standards.
Build strong relationships with clinical services and operational leaders to coordinate maintenance activities with minimal disruption.
Manage contractor performance, site safety and compliance across facilities.
Monitor operational performance, maintenance budgets and key service delivery indicators.
Drive continuous improvement in facilities operations, maintenance practices and customer service.
Support emergency response activities and ensure operational readiness across sites.
Collaborate with engineering, infrastructure and capital project teams to support maintenance and operational priorities.
Contribute to sustainability initiatives and operational improvements across the health service.



About You


To be successful in this role, you will bring:


Extensive experience leading facilities management or engineering operations within a large, complex organisation.
Strong operational leadership experience managing maintenance services, building operations and critical infrastructure.
Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Experience working closely with operational stakeholders to deliver customer-focused facilities services.
Sound knowledge of statutory compliance, essential services maintenance and contractor management.
Strong financial management skills, including budget oversight and resource planning.
Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement and problem-solving abilities.
The ability to remain calm and make effective decisions in a fast-paced operational environment.



Why you will love working with us 


Ours is a connected team with strong shared values and an unwavering commitment to excellence. We are a highly skilled, collaborative, and welcoming team where the only limit in your career is you. Upon your appointment, we will provide you with 



A supportive and cohesive sub-team, working within a larger consumer relations team. 


Professional development courses, seminars and mentoring. 


Opportunities for you to use your experience in the role to inform and drive initiatives within the broader units and programs. 


Salary packaging. 


Onsite Gym options and ability to join Fitness Passport - your pass to an extensive choice of fitness facilities. 




For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Linda Byron - Administrative Lead to the Head of Engineering & Facilities Management, via email at Linda.Byron@monashhealth.org.



Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 







Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 







You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 







We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 







We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply


Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'


Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your role at St John of God Midland Private Hospital

This is an exciting opportunity to join St John of God Midland Private Hospital at the opening of the hospital in August 2026. We are seeking an experienced and motivated Clinical Nurse Scrub-Scout General Surgical to help shape high quality patient care within a modern, purpose-built environment. 

You will be part of a founding clinical team, contributing to the establishment of best practice models of care while delivering safe, effective and patient centred critical care services. 

The Position

Supervise clinical practice of all caregivers taking responsibility for standard of care delivered.

Initiate reviews and coordinate care of patients with complex health problems.

Serves as a patient advocate, protecting the rights and safety of patients at all times.

Actively contributes to the development of clinical policies and procedures in area of specialty.

Responsible and accountable for nominated portfolios as designated by Nurse Unit Manager and actively communicate with Nurse Unit Manager regarding updates.

Participate in and takes responsibility for the education of other caregivers by conducting formal and informal teaching sessions.

Systematically evaluate actions and document the outcomes of nursing-medical interventions (including monitoring diagnostic results) and report significant anomalies promptly.

Ensure documentation of planned nursing care and holistic care plan remains current and regularly evaluate documentation of the multidisciplinary team to determine their compliance to hospital policy.

Prioritise departmental workloads using resources appropriately and cost effectively.

Assist the Nurse Unit Manager with the submission of annual capital budget and business plans relevant to the Department.

Review products and equipment and provides documentation and education on evaluation.

Assist in developing, implementing and reviewing specific departmental orientation programs with Nurse Unit Manager, acts as a preceptor as required.

Participate in Manager Meetings as well as relevant committees and working parties as required.

Act as shift coordinator as required and in liaison with the Nurse - After Hours Manager- Perioperative flow manager and monitor staffing levels continuously to ensure appropriate numbers of skilled staff are available within the agreed productivity targets.

Contribute to planning, problem solving and change management within the Nursing Division throughout the hospital as required.

Liaise with the multidisciplinary team, to ensure effective use of human and material ward resources and coordinated inter departmental activities.

Develop and maintain effective relationships with relevant internal and external key Stakeholders to build and enhance service delivery on a divisional and group-wide basis.

In collaboration with Nurse Unit Manager and Human Resources, monitor and promote adherence by caregivers to hospital policies, procedures and standards. Assist with managing performance concerns.

Conduct Performance reviews and development (PR&D) plans as directed by the Nurse Unit Manager.

In collaboration with the Nurse Unit Manager, support and coordinate clinical audits to ensure compliance with standards, guidelines, and best practice.

Assist Nurse Unit Manager with the analysis of audit findings and work with the team to implement improvement strategies.

All other reasonable duties as directed by the relevant Manager-Supervisor

You will hold registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia as a Registered Nurse and have significant recent post registration experience and the ability to practice at an advanced level.

To succeed you will have well developed leadership and communication skills and an ability to effectively engage with a range of senior and operational stakeholders.

About the new Midland Private Hospital 

A brand-new purpose-built state-of-the-art facility, currently under construction, located just 300 metres from the St John of God Midland Public and Private Hospitals Campus. 

A comprehensive range of medical and surgical services, with interventional cardiology being offered for the first time in the region

 The hospital will feature:

96 overnight inpatient beds, including a six-bed critical care-high dependency unit

33 bed-chair short stay and day procedure unit

Eight operating theatres

A Cardiac Catheter Laboratory

We can offer you

Salary: $109,599 to $115,681 (pro rata for part time) plus 12% superannuation

Permanent part time (0.65 FTE)

Salary packaging up to $18,550 on a range of benefits such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses as well as options to salary package benefits above the FBT cap on items such as:

Novated leasing 

work related expenses

self-education and

additional superannuation

A healthy work-life balance through flexible work options, additional purchased leave and well-being programs

Employee discount on St John of God Hospital & Medical Services and Private Health Insurance

Employee support through our dedicated free Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Access to fitness and wellbeing benefits through Fitness Passport

All applicants are asked to submit a covering letter (of no more than two (2) pages) demonstrating how you meet the above position requirements.

For enquiries, please contact Chanel Armstrong, Acting Manager Perioperative Services on 0457 534 689

Applications close 15th July 2026

If suitable applicants are identified the advertisement may close prior to listed date and screening-interviews may commence throughout the advertising process.

At St John of God Health Care, we celebrate diversity and warmly welcome applications from people of all backgrounds.

Our commitment is to create a safe and nurturing environment for all children and vulnerable individuals in our care and proactively take steps to protect them from abuse, ensuring their safety and well-being.

Our inclusive culture fosters an environment that is respectful and secure, welcoming and accessible, and unified through our diverse community.    Click here to Apply now →

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 


We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 


As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 


Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.





Senior Digital Business Analyst




Care, reimagined


Design and deliver innovative learning that builds clinical digital capability


Permanent, full time role, hybrid workplace model




Shape the Digital Future of Healthcare Across Victoria.




Great digital systems only deliver when they are designed around the real-world needs of the people using them. This newly created role is about bridging the gap between clinical reality and digital innovation-translating complex organizational and frontline needs into practical, high-impact digital solutions that move Monash Health toward genuine service transformation.





Make a Difference Through Digital Health


About The Role



We are now seeking an experienced and passionate Senior Digital Business Analyst to join our Innovation, Platforms and Partnership team within the Digital and Information Division.



This is an opportunity to work on some of Victoria's most significant digital health initiatives, helping transform the way care is delivered across clinical and non-clinical services. You will work alongside project managers, clinicians, technical specialists, operational leaders and executives to design solutions that improve patient care, streamline services and deliver meaningful outcomes for our community.



We are looking for someone who values teamwork, thrives on solving complex problems, and wants to contribute to projects that have a genuine impact on the lives of patients, families and healthcare staff.



You will lead business analysis activities from project initiation through to solution implementation, working closely with stakeholders to understand business needs, identify opportunities for improvement and help deliver practical, sustainable solutions.



You will also:





Lead stakeholder engagement, workshops and requirements gathering activities across clinical and corporate services.


Develop business cases, project initiation documentation and solution proposals that support organisational priorities


Analyse business processes, workflows and service models to identify improvement opportunities and deliver measurable benefits


Work closely with technical teams to translate business requirements into effective digital solutions.


Support solution design, testing, implementation and change activities across complex projects.


Contribute to portfolio planning, resource management and prioritisation activities across a diverse digital project portfolio.






What We're Looking For



We are seeking a collaborative and community-minded professional who enjoys working with others to achieve shared outcomes.



You will bring:





Extensive experience as a Senior Business Analyst within large and complex environments.


Strong stakeholder engagement, facilitation and communication skills with the ability to build trusted relationships at all levels of an organisation.


Experience preparing business cases, analysing business processes and developing solution recommendations.


Demonstrated ability to lead workshops, manage competing priorities and influence outcomes in complex environments.


Experience working across both Agile and Waterfall delivery environments.


A proactive, solutions-focused approach and a commitment to delivering outcomes that improve services for our patients and community.





Experience in healthcare or digital health is highly regarded.






Why join Monash Health?



This is more than a digital role-it's your chance to transform healthcare at scale. Working at the intersection of clinical care, technology and innovation, you'll help create smarter digital solutions that improve patient outcomes and support the clinicians who deliver them every day




At Monash Health, you will:






Lead a state-wide service with real impact


Work within a values-driven, purpose-led organisation


Be part of a connected network of clinical, academic and system leaders


Help drive innovation, inclusion and better health outcomes








We also offer:






The opportunity to make a real impact on patient experience


A supportive, collaborative team environment


Ongoing learning and development opportunities


The chance to be part of Victoria's largest public health service






For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to 


Monica Lenko- Head of Digital Delivery - Monica.Lenko@monashhealth.org



To view the Position Description, click the link below


# # 8673 Senior Business Analyst PD.docx





Our Culture and Values 



At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 



Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 



You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 




We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 



We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 




If you're passionate about helping clinicians embrace digital innovation and want to influence the future of healthcare at scale, we'd love to hear from you.




Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'



Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.

Digital Marketing & E-commerce Manager  
   
  St Leonards, Sydney | Hybrid (1-2 days WFH) | $170k inclusive super + 10% STI  
   
  The Role:  
   
  This is a well-established, product-led business in the health, beauty and wellbeing space, with a strong retail/clinic network and a fast-growing digital and eCommerce arm. As they continue to scale their online presence, they're looking for a   Digital Marketing & E-commerce Manager   to take ownership of digital growth and bring real strategic rigour to the function.  
   
 This is a standalone position reporting directly to the Head of Digital. You won't be managing a team - instead, you'll be hands-on, resourceful, and the driving force behind the organisation's digital sales growth. You'll bring the discipline and structure of a larger organisation into a business that's ready to professionalise its digital function further. 
   
  Responsibilities : 
   
 
  Own the performance of the online marketplace and brand websites, driving traffic, conversion, AOV and repeat purchase.  
  Lead the digital media investment strategy across paid social, search, programmatic and affiliate, with clear accountability for ROI and attribution.  
  CRM is central to this role. You'll own database growth, segmentation, automated lifecycle journeys, and loyalty programs that drive retention.  
  Own the digital promotional calendar and digital-specific campaign levers, briefing and guiding creative development.  
  Drive organic visibility and continuous CRO/UX improvement across digital properties.  
  Work closely with Sales, Brand, Customer Service and the wider retail/clinic network to ensure digital activity supports, rather than competes with the broader business.  
  Provide meaningful input into broader digital strategy and commercial planning, working closely with the Head of Digital.  
 
   
  What we're looking for:  
   
 
  Prior experience in Shopify (preferred but not essential)  
  Experience in a   product-based business  , ideally within healthcare, wellbeing, beauty or a related consumer space.  
  A confident individual owning database growth, segmentation and lifecycle automation.  
  A track record in digital marketing and eCommerce, with solid commercial and analytical acumen.  
  Excellent   stakeholder management   skills and able to build trust and influence across a diverse business.  
  Comfortable owning a standalone function without a team around you.  
  Ideally, you've worked within a larger, more structured organisation and can bring that discipline to a growing business.  
  Looking for a step up in your career, ready to take full ownership of a high-impact, high-visibility role.

Position Summary
Training Officers work in a dynamic vocational, education and training environment in which they have to adapt and be responsive to changes in national curriculum, the VET Quality Framework, technological developments and a diversity and breadth of client training demands.

The role of the Training Officer embraces the extent of the learning process from program enquiry/advice through to assessing and determining the training requirements of clients, following onto managing the learning process for clients using a variety of training strategies including recognition of prior learning, recognition of current competencies, training delivery, workplace learning, delivery and assessment, formal assessment and reporting etc..  

The training Officer will have the vocational skills in the area that they are applying for with a minimum of three to five years’ experience in their chosen vocational area.

The Training Officer ideally would have at least have obtained the following competencies from the Training and Assessment Training Package or is able to demonstrate equivalent competencies. However if the candidate does not have these competencies or the full Training & Assessment Qualification they will agree to work with an accredited assessor until this qualification is achieved.

The Training Officer is expected to be innovative in responding effectively to the training demands of clients.  The Training Officer works in a wide variety of learning environments providing a range of flexible training and learning strategies to best meet the client needs including flexible delivery, workplace training and assessment, training room delivery, on line learning support etc.   

The Training Officer will be expected to be able to work effectively as a member of a team and be required to be involved in a range of course/program coordination and administration activities that support the effective operation of the company and the achievement of learning outcomes for participants.  

POSITION PARAMETERS
1.	SUPERVISION AND ACCOUNTABILITY The position reports to the Manager and may work in a number of program areas. 
2.	LOCATION Training Staff are required to work on site or at a designated training facility.  
3.	PARTICIPATION ON COMMITTEES Training Officers are required to attend program meetings and team meetings, or other external committees as required.

Duty Statement
1.	Develop and manage the learning process for participants. 
2.	Train in a range of subjects and programs in a variety of learning modes at locations specified by the Manager. (See Attachment 1 for position details)
3.	Prepare quality learning and assessment resources within the context of established curriculum, training packages under the national framework, competency standards, the diversity of students and client’s requirements. Unless otherwise agreed with the Training Officer, Intellectual Property in all material developed or produced shall remain within Industry Training & Workplace Services.
4.	Participate as a member of a team on a range of tasks including curriculum and program development, program delivery, professional development, marketing activities and administrative and operational functions.
5.	Undertake, where required, course coordination and a range of planning tasks relevant to the delivery of quality courses.
6.	Provide support and advice to participants of diverse cultures, backgrounds and abilities and implement appropriate support strategies and/or learning programs and strategies as required.
7.	Undertake as required a range of participant support service tasks to ensure the effective operation of the Company, for example participant selection, course advice, enrolment and telephone enquiry support.
8.	Research, adapt and develop innovative learning practices and delivery options that enhance the Company's capacity to meet the demands of participants. 
9.	Manage the delivery of training services to industry, including workplace visits, assessing training needs, developing training plans and coordinating the effective delivery of programs.
10.	Participate in and contribute to the development and implementation of evaluation and continuous improvement processes across the Company.
11.	Undertake regular professional development to maintain and continuously improve individual professional and vocational competencies as a Training Officer.
12.	Comply with the quality assurance requirements of the Australian Quality Training Framework and the company’s Quality System.

SELECTION CRITERIA 
Qualifications
1.	The minimum training qualification is the Certificate IV in Training & Assessment or equivalent. 
2.	It is mandatory to have relevant vocational competence at or higher than the level being delivered or assessed through having qualifications and/or relevant industry experience. 
3.	Training Officers who do not hold the minimum or equivalent training qualification must undertake professional development to gain the training qualification within 12 months of commencement. In the interim, the training officer must agree to be mentored by a qualified Trainer who does hold the minimum or equivalent qualification

Training Excellence
1.	Demonstrated excellence in training, management of learning and assessment.
2.	Demonstrated experience in contributing to development of learning resources.
3.	 An understanding of current developments and innovative approaches in training.
4.	Demonstrated experience, or ability to, develop and conduct training programs suitable to the needs of industry.
5.	Demonstrated record of innovation in training and proven commitment to undertake regular professional development to maintain and continuously improve individual professional competence.

Communication Skills
1.	Proven ability to operate effectively as a member of a team.
2.	High level interpersonal and communication skills.
3.	Demonstrated ability to provide support and advice to students of diverse cultures, backgrounds and abilities.
Administration
1.	High level organisational skills
2.	Demonstrated experience in contributing to the overall functioning of the company including record keeping, course maintenance and quality improvement and ability to use all relevant technology.

Further Information
For further information please contact Toni Hoyle.
Telephone 90227100 or 0419 908 425
